record.title: CS/CS/HB 1159 (2026): Sexual Offenses
record.short_title: Florida HB 1159 (2026): sexual offences and generated CSAM
record.issuing_body: Florida Legislature (2026 Regular Session; sponsors Judiciary Committee, Criminal Justice Subcommittee and Rep. Jacques); approved by the Governor
record.summary: Replaces 'child pornography' with 'child sexual abuse material' in Florida statutes, raises penalties and sets mandatory minimum sentences for child sexual abuse material and child sexual performance offences, and creates a life felony for using a child under 12 in a sexual performance. For computer-generated imagery, it raises the offence of creating generated child sexual abuse material, an image made or modified by computer-generated means to portray a fictitious person whom a reasonable person would regard as a real minor engaged in sexual conduct, from a third- to a second-degree felony, and makes transmitting such material within, into or out of Florida a second-degree felony.
record.notes: Passed the House 105-0 on 3 Mar 2026 and the Senate 37-0 on 9 Mar 2026, where it was substituted for CS/SB 1750; approved by the Governor on 31 Mar 2026 and effective 1 Jul 2026. Section 9 amends s. 827.072, F.S., the generated child pornography offence created in 2024 by CS/CS/SB 1680 (ch. 2024-118). The companion terminology bill CS/HB 245 (ch. 2026-18) also passed. Other provisions raise penalties for possessing a child-like sex doll and for sexual activities involving animals, and bar people convicted of the latter from owning or working with animals for at least five years.
record.scope_note: Not an AI-specific law: an omnibus sexual offences act. Included because it raises the penalty for creating computer-generated child sexual abuse material and makes transmitting it a crime, amending the offence created by Florida's 2024 Advanced Technology law.

verification.note: Stored the Florida Senate bill page for HB 1159 (2026) and two House staff analyses linked from it (flsenate.gov), including the final bill analysis of 1 Apr 2026. The bill page confirms the title, sponsors, history, floor votes (105-0 and 37-0), approval by the Governor on 31 Mar 2026, Chapter No. 2026-20 and the 1 Jul 2026 effective date; the final analysis confirms approval, chapter and effective date and describes the enacted provisions, including section 9 on generated child sexual abuse material, on which the summary rests. The statement that s. 827.072 was created by CS/CS/SB 1680 rests on the Senate analysis stored for candidate C002. The enrolled bill text was not stored.

judgment.status_reasoning: Approved by the Governor on 31 Mar 2026 (Chapter No. 2026-20) with an effective date of 1 Jul 2026. Today (14 Oct 2026) is after that date, so in force. The stored files show no later amendment.
judgment.scope_reasoning: Borderline, included with a scope_note under the rule for laws that are not AI-specific but are the operative instrument for an AI-safety question: an omnibus sexual offences act whose section 9 sets the current penalties for creating and transmitting computer-generated child sexual abuse material. Follows the treatment of US-CA-13 (California SB 1276), a general child-exploitation law included with a scope_note for its AI-generated material provisions.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the Governor's approval (31 Mar 2026); date_in_force the stated effective date (1 Jul 2026). The chapter number was assigned on 1 Apr 2026.
judgment.related_reasoning: C002 (CS/CS/SB 1680, 2024) created s. 827.072, which section 9 of this act amends. US-CA-13 is a comparable state law bringing AI-generated child sexual abuse material within existing offences.
